steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Latin word order is much freer than English because grammatical relationships are shown by case endings, not position. The most common order is Subject-Object-Verb (SOV). | Key Fact: The verb typically comes at or near the end of a Latin sentence, which is the biggest difference from English SVO order. | Key Fact: Adjectives must agree with the noun they modify in gender, number, and case (GNC): puella bona (good girl, fem. nom. sg.), servum bonum (good slave, masc. acc. sg.). | Key Fact: Relative clauses use the relative pronoun qui, quae, quod (who, which, that) which must agree with its antecedent in gender and number, but takes its case from its own clause.
